items.title: Robinhood event contract revenue rises more than sixfold to 173 million dollars in the third quarter on a record 16.4 billion contracts traded, The Street reports
items.content_text: - **Robinhood event contract revenue rises more than sixfold to 173 million dollars in the third quarter on a record 16.4 billion contracts traded, The Street reports** — The Street reports Robinhood said third-quarter event contract revenue rose more than sixfold year over year to 173 million dollars, ahead of crypto revenue of 120 million dollars, as customers traded a record 16.4 billion event contracts, more than seven times the year-earlier count. Non-sports contracts, including elections, accounted for roughly 30 percent of prediction market activity, up from about 15 percent in the previous quarter, and Robinhood launched a dedicated U.S. Midterms Hub in September for congressional control and other election contracts. (The Street)

items.title: CFTC and Justice Department sue Utah to block state enforcement against Kalshi, their tenth state case and the first against a Republican-led state, SCCG reports
items.content_text: - **CFTC and Justice Department sue Utah to block state enforcement against Kalshi, their tenth state case and the first against a Republican-led state, SCCG reports** — SCCG reports the CFTC and the Department of Justice filed a 33-page federal complaint seeking to stop Utah Attorney General Derek Brown from applying state gambling restrictions, election betting prohibitions or public nuisance laws to CFTC-registered exchanges, after Utah sued Kalshi and two Susquehanna trading firms on October 20. items.title: Intercontinental Exchange carries its Polymarket stake at about 2.0 billion dollars, roughly 22 percent of the platform's outstanding shares, PR Newswire reports
items.content_text: - **Intercontinental Exchange carries its Polymarket stake at about 2.0 billion dollars, roughly 22 percent of the platform's outstanding shares, PR Newswire reports** — PR Newswire reports Intercontinental Exchange, owner of the New York Stock Exchange, said in its third-quarter filing that the carrying value of its Series D and E preferred stock investments in Polymarket was approximately 2.0 billion dollars as of September 30, representing about 22 percent of Polymarket's outstanding shares and 14 percent on a fully diluted basis.
